Articles must be supported by research or a systematic approach; reviews require critical synthesis that provides an original perspective or new understanding. Provisional agent judgment within generalist STS: editors explicitly desk-reject work lacking scope alignment, broad STS usefulness, readable presentation or adequate argument. Research articles must engage STS and be interesting beyond a narrow specialty, followed ordinarily by at least two external reports. This broad-contribution gate supports high difficulty without a measured acceptance rate. Its restrictive genAI expectations are a separate manuscript-fit condition, not evidence that all AI-assisted work is banned.

Official acceptance criteria require research quality, originality and scientific significance, with at least two reviews and statistical review where needed. Original articles and other specified types may be unsolicited; reviews and several other types are commissioned or invited. These establish a real scholarly bar, but the displayed rolling acceptance statistic lacks a defined population and exact window dates, so a comparative difficulty band is left unknown.

notes: All 13 unique discovery and diamond candidates were independently considered after reading the fee audit. This file supplies only difficulty and metric replacements; it does not change fees, publication models, eligibility, formats or review labels.

Difficulty bands are explicit provisional agent judgments about the editorial bar within each venue's scholarly community. Meta-research is a navigational cluster spanning bibliometrics, evaluation, STS, ethics, evidence-synthesis methods and scholarly publishing; these are not one interchangeable prestige ladder. Very high is used here only with unusually selective official final-decision data plus a documented contribution/scope gate. No band is an acceptance probability for an individual manuscript.

Only non-null, officially reported metric values with a retained period are structured. Citation metrics use exact displayed years and established provider definitions; actual numerator/denominator counts are not supplied. Missing statistics are not zero and do not mean easy acceptance. No third-party journal-metric aggregator values were adopted.

Sage's journal pages show SSS 7.7%, Research Ethics 21.9% and JIS 4.6% without adjacent year labels. The publisher's live definition states previous calendar year and all article types receiving final accept/reject decisions; at the 2026-11-16 check that identifies 2025. This period identification is an inference from the documented definition, not a year printed next to each journal rate. The rates are neither submission-cohort probabilities nor externally-reviewed-only proportions.

Accountability in Research's official indexed About page reports 13% acceptance, JIF 4.4, 5-year JIF 4.1 and CiteScore 6.4, with citation year 2025. Its page was blocked on direct access, so these are explicitly search-indexed-source observations. Taylor & Francis's accessible definition identifies acceptance rates as previous full calendar year, refreshed in February, and includes all final decisions/article types plus desk rejections. Reverify the rate/value page before consequential use.

Scientometrics displays median submission-to-first-decision 26 days without a period or explicit review-stage denominator in the inspected journal display; it is omitted from metrics. Its 2025 citation metrics do not establish selectivity.

Research Evaluation's author-guidelines page retains 2024 JIF 2.5 and CiteScore 5.7. The current homepage/About metrics agree on 2025 JIF 2.7 and CiteScore 3.6; the structured values preserve that newer explicitly labeled period instead of relabeling the older author-guidelines figures.

Research Synthesis Methods' current Cambridge homepage explicitly reports 2025 JIF 8. Its metrics table also displays 5-year JIF 14.3, CiteScore 12.1, Eigenfactor .01194, Article Influence 4.799, SJR 3.143 and SNIP 2.967 without metric years in the inspected table; those undated values are not added to structured metrics. The same live HTML explicitly retains Wiley's historical 2023 acceptance rate 31%, first decision 13 days and submission-to-acceptance 215 days. Only the historical acceptance rate is structured, with Wiley's final-decision definition. None of these historical measures establishes the current Cambridge OA fee route; the fee audit's current-publisher distinction is preserved.

Meta-Psychology does not use novelty or a desired rejection percentage as selection criteria; this is not a 100% acceptance-rate claim. Its About page says preregistration is encouraged rather than mandatory, while the specific current submission checklist requires it for studies collecting primary or secondary data, including metascience/literature reviews, and for confirmatory research questions/hypotheses. The stricter operative checklist is retained as the submission condition. OSF sharing, a suitable DOI-bearing preprint and applicable reproducibility checks remain substantial obligations. Its undated TOP Factor 27 and Nordic List level are not structured as year-qualified metrics.

ESTS's broad STS contribution requirement is independent of its genAI policy. The policy strongly discourages generative AI except unavailable-alternative translation or when genAI forms the empirical/analytical focus; it requires all use disclosed in the cover letter and data-generation/analysis use described in the manuscript. It reserves editorial judgment about a meaningful STS contribution. The FAQ's undated 'not yet' impact-factor answer is not treated as a verified current absence of a JIF, and no numeric official metric was established.

Science Editing's directly retrieved homepage reports 26% acceptance and marks the statistic 'Last 12 months', but does not state the underlying decision population or exact start/end dates. This value stays in notes rather than a dated metric. The instructions' normal four-week first-decision aim is a service target, not measured performance. The explicit completed-year 2025 CiteScore 2.1 is structured.

European Science Editing's directly retrieved instructions report approximately 50% acceptance without year, population or counts; this stays in notes. Its homepage labels CiteScore 2025 as 3.0 and CiteScoreTracker 2026 as 1.9, updated monthly; only the completed-year metric is structured. Homepage JIF 1.6 has no adjacent year in the inspected text and is omitted from structured metrics.

No official numeric acceptance or year-qualified citation value was established for LIBER Quarterly or Meta-Psychology in the inspected sources. Their empty metric arrays record missing evidence, not poor quality. Science Editing and European Science Editing HTML were retrieved as full live pages by direct HTTP despite browser-access failures; these observations are stronger than snippets.

An official Research Ethics PDF snapshot at https://www.sagepub.com/docs/default-source/msg/submission-guidelines_-research-ethics_-sage-journals.pdf retains older APC wording and an undated JIF 2.2; current author-guidelines indexed HTML describes Community Open Access. The undated PDF JIF is not reused, and no fee field is patched. Current policy pages should take precedence over an unversioned snapshot only with its conflict preserved.

Checked on 2026-11-16 using official journal/publisher material, with access and historical-source limits recorded above. This is an agent research audit, not human scientific review, an endorsement, or a submission recommendation for a specific manuscript.
